newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Futures fell shaky Australian stocks by close.
newsitem.headline: Futures fell shaky Australian stocks by close.

text.p: Australian shares closed lower on Tuesday, the market slipping away in the afternoon in line with a rapidly fading futures market.
The All Ordinaries index lost 23.1 points to 2,404.3.

Media major News Corp was the featured loser among the leaders as traders voiced their disapproval of the company's US$1.35 billion Heritage buy. Its shares closed 3.3 percent lower at A$6.36 (US$5.02).

Yesterday's big losers, the Papua New Guinea-linked stocks, recouped some of Monday's losses as fears over political instability in the country diminished, although they eased off their highs with the broader market by the close.

Government-controlled mining investor Orogen Minerals dived 22 cents to an intraday low of A$2.98 before finding support and climbing to a high of A$3.26. It then eased with the broader market to end steady at A$3.20. Oil Search ended up 10 cents at A$2.70, Lihir Gold shares closed up two cents at A$2.12, while Niugini Mining added four cents to A$3.00.
The broader market was set for a rangebound day until the last hour of trading when sellers slugged the March share futures contract, dragging the underlying market down with it.

"Futures came off in the last hour or so and that cut most of them back," said a Sydney-based broker, adding that nerves over Wall Street appeared to be the likely cause given the dearth of local news.
"I can only put it down to U.S. concerns. There are still some worries over there."
Others also noted the lack of local impetus, saying the market ran out of puff in the afternoon.
"It slowed down quite a bit and was a very patchy day," said a dealer at a Perth brokerage.
Packaging group Amcor weighed on the index, going ex-dividend 18 cents and closing 32 cents lower at A$8.28. Golds also disappointed, the gold index losing 1.9 percent.

Grand Hotel Group topped turnover lists with 39.7 million securities traded, the bulk of it in one line through County Natwest Securities at A$2.05 per share. Brokers said the trade appeared to be the 39 percent stake acquired by Singapore group Tuan Sing Holdings in January, the purchase was which was approved by Grand Hotel shareholders on March 11.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
